output.brief: What is going on: the departures are concentrated in the Kestrel review team, not spread across the group. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel resigned, against one of 13 others. Kestrel associates also record about 2,270 hours a year, against about 1,940 for the rest of the group, with weekend work on 31% of weekends versus 6%. Pay, the firm-wide billable target and general market mobility do not fit this pattern. The main open question is whether the cause is the workload or the supervision. Every Kestrel associate reports to the same partner, Dorian Faulk, so the records cannot separate the two. My confidence that workload is the main driver is moderate, and the supervision question is unresolved. Next: run the confidential interviews (about £9k, within three weeks) structured to separate supervision from workload. Do not pay the group-wide retention payment or close the review yet, because that would spend money on the wrong cause and end the inquiry. Start recording matter and supervisor data for attrition now. Interventions for the workload itself can be prepared in parallel.
